metaData.originalTitle: The Strange Logic of World Cup Ticket Prices
metaData.title: The Strange Logic of World Cup Ticket Prices
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: By analyzing resale ticket prices, this article reveals that host country pride, aging superstars Messi and Ronaldo, and Latin American diaspora demand drive World Cup ticket prices, while European teams underperform due to travel costs and immigration policies.
metaData.summary: This analysis by three economists examines the 2026 FIFA World Cup group-stage ticket resale market (StubHub) to uncover what drives fan demand. By isolating team and city effects from the lowest single-ticket prices, the authors find that host nations (Mexico, US, Canada) command huge premiums, as do teams featuring Lionel Messi (Argentina) and Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal). Brazil retains strong appeal. In contrast, traditional European powers (England, Germany, France, Netherlands) have negative estimated team effects, likely because European fans face high costs and stricter border policies. City effects show Miami and Mexican host cities dominate, while West Coast venues underperform. The authors also note that the data reflects pre-tournament expectations and has limitations, but provides a rare window into North American soccer fandom shaped by patriotism, immigration, and geography.

mainPoints.point: Host nations and Latin American teams command the highest resale premiums.
mainPoints.explanation: Mexico adds $623, the US $571, and Canada $231 to the cheapest ticket price. Brazil adds $299, Argentina $312, and Portugal $442, reflecting diaspora demand and superstar appeal.

mainPoints.point: Aging superstars Messi and Ronaldo are the sport's biggest draws, surpassing younger stars.
mainPoints.explanation: Their teams generate multi-hundred-dollar premiums, driven by their global celebrity status and the sense of witnessing history.

mainPoints.point: European powers show resale price premiums below zero, suggesting weaker demand from European fans.
mainPoints.explanation: High travel costs, tough U.S. immigration enforcement, and smaller expatriate communities in North America likely deter European supporters.

mainPoints.point: City effects vary dramatically, with Miami and Mexican host cities exceeding $800 premiums over Kansas City.
mainPoints.explanation: Miami's Latin American ties and high tourism make it the most expensive venue, while West Coast cities like San Francisco show negative city effects due to geography and travel distances.

keyQuotes: Resale prices reveal what soccer fans, both domestic and foreign, are most excited to see---or at least, what sellers believe fans desire most intensely.

A supporter in Germany or England can ordinarily reach all the European Championship matches---or the next World Cup in Morocco, Spain, and Portugal---with a short flight or train journey. A tournament spread across North America presents a fundamentally different proposition.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article argues that the recent U.S.-Iran truce, like the Gaza deal before it, only defers hard questions and sets the stage for prolonged low-intensity conflict rather than lasting peace.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This essay traces the evolution of political trolling from its origins in early internet message boards to its current role as a dominant, right-leaning force in U.S. politics, arguing it is a sadistic, non-educative form of provocation that has reshaped conservatism and polarized the electorate.
